name: Cessna 182 Skylane
summary: Heavier, more powerful four-seat sibling of the 172, popular for cross-country flying, Civil Air Patrol and skydiving.

wings: High wing braced by a single lift strut per side
Same planform family as the smaller four-seat high-wing, slightly larger
engines: Big six-cylinder engine in a deep, blunt cowling with cowl flaps at the rear
Constant-speed prop with large spinner; three-blade common on later models
fuselage: Wider, deeper four-seat cabin with wraparound rear window
Fixed tricycle gear with a shorter, sturdier nose strut
Overall heavier, more robust look than the 172

tellTales: Strut-braced high wing with a deep, chunky nose cowl
Three-blade prop and large spinner on many examples
Cowl flaps visible at the lower rear of the cowling

confusedWith.howToTell: The 182 has a deeper, blunter cowling, larger spinner and often a three-blade prop; the 172's nose is slimmer with a two-blade prop.
The 206 has a longer cabin with an extra window and a large double cargo door on the right; the 182 has a shorter cabin with one door per side.
The 180/185 is a taildragger; the 182 has a nose wheel.
The Skymaster has two engines (one in the nose, one pusher behind the cabin) and twin tail booms; the 182 has one engine and a single fin.
The 182 has a lift strut and a deeper, blunter cowl; the 177 Cardinal has a strutless wing, a smoother nose and a one-piece stabilator.
The 182 has a flat engine, a lift strut and (mostly) a nosewheel; the 195 has a big radial engine, no struts and a tailwheel.
